31662-their-son-the-necklace.description: A book by Eduardo Zamacois. To me, Zamacois seems a Spanish Guy de Maupassant. He tells a story in much the same way, with that grace and charm which only genius, coupled to infinite hard work, can crystallize on the printed page. His subjects are often much the same as those of de Maupassant.

arxiv-2103-09891.title: The Untapped Potential of Off-the-Shelf Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2103-09891.creator: Matthew Inkawhich, Nathan Inkawhich, Eric Davis, Yiran Chen
arxiv-2103-09891.description: Abstract Over recent years, a myriad of novel convolutional network architectures have been developed to advance state-of-the-art performance on challenging recognition tasks. As computational resources improve, a great deal of effort has been placed in efficiently scaling up existing designs and generating new architectures with Neural Architecture Search (NAS) algorithms.

arxiv-2105-04090.title: MuseMorphose: Full-Song and Fine-Grained Piano Music Style Transfer with One Transformer VAE
arxiv-2105-04090.creator: Shih-Lun Wu, and Yi-Hsuan Yang
arxiv-2105-04090.description: Abstract Transformers and variational autoencoders (VAE) have been extensively employed for symbolic (e.g., MIDI) domain music generation. While the former boast an impressive capability in modeling long sequences, the latter allow users to willingly exert control over different parts (e.g., bars) of the music to be generated.

arxiv-2106-10795.title: Large-scale image segmentation based on distributed clustering algorithms
arxiv-2106-10795.creator: Ran Lu, Aleksandar Zlateski, H. Sebastian Seung
arxiv-2106-10795.description: Abstract Many approaches to 3D image segmentation are based on hierarchical clustering of supervoxels into image regions. Here we describe a distributed algorithm capable of handling a tremendous number of supervoxels. The algorithm works recursively, the regions are divided into chunks that are processed independently in parallel by multiple workers.

arxiv-2112-01109.title: Electron excitation rate in dielectrics under an intense elliptically polarized laser field
arxiv-2112-01109.creator: Prachi Venkat and Tomohito Otobe
arxiv-2112-01109.description: Abstract Electron excitation in dielectrics is studied for an elliptically polarized laser field. As the first step, we develop an analytical formula for electron excitation rate under elliptically polarized laser as the extension of our previous work [T. Otobe et. al. , JPSJ 88 (2019) 024709].

arxiv-2207-10151.title: Tackling the infamous g 6 g^{6} term of the QCD pressure
arxiv-2207-10151.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by *. We report on ongoing efforts to tackle an important open problem in QCD thermodynamics, namely an evaluation of the pressure to order g 6 g^{6} in a weak-coupling expansion, corresponding to four loops. In particular, we identify a class of contributing Feynman sum-integrals with lower-loop factors, describe the formalism to tensor decompose those, and manage to map them onto scalar master sum-integrals that have already been evaluated in the literature.

arxiv-2410-20455.title: Role of non-magnetic spacers in the magnetic interactions of antiferromagnetic topological insulators MnBi 4 Te 7 and MnBi 2 Te 4
arxiv-2410-20455.creator: Bing Li, D. M. Pajerowski, J.-Q. Yan, R. J. McQueeney
arxiv-2410-20455.description: Abstract MnBi 4 Te 7 belongs to a family of antiferromagnetic topological insulators. It forms a natural heterostructure of magnetic (septuple) and non-magnetic (quintuple) topological blocks. Here, we explore the magnetism and magnetic interactions in this compound using inelastic neutron scattering.

arxiv-2508-05001.title: CRAM: Large-scale Video Continual Learning with Bootstrapped Compression
arxiv-2508-05001.creator: Shivani Mall, João F. Henriques
arxiv-2508-05001.description: Abstract Continual learning (CL) promises to allow neural networks to learn from continuous streams of inputs, instead of IID (independent and identically distributed) sampling, which requires random access to a full dataset. This would allow for much smaller storage requirements and self-sufficiency of deployed systems that cope with natural distribution shifts, similarly to biological learning.

arxiv-2508-08529.title: SynLLM: A Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models for Medical Tabular Synthetic Data Generation via Prompt Engineering
arxiv-2508-08529.creator: Arshia Ilaty 1 , Hossein Shirazi 2 , Hajar Homayouni 2
arxiv-2508-08529.description: Abstract Access to real-world medical data is often restricted due to privacy regulations, posing a significant barrier to the advancement of healthcare research. Synthetic data offers a promising alternative; however, generating realistic, clinically valid, and privacy-conscious records remains a major challenge.

arxiv-2509-24287.title: Lifshitz transition in a holographic finite density flavour brane Weyl semimetal
arxiv-2509-24287.creator: Cheng-Yuan Lu 1 , Xian-Hui Ge 1,2∗ , Sang-Jin Sin 3
arxiv-2509-24287.description: Abstract We extend a top-down holographic model of a Weyl semimetal to finite charge density and compute the fermionic spectral function by introducing two probe fermions of opposite chirality. The model is controlled by the boundary fermion mass M M and the chemical potential μ \mu .

arxiv-2510-02951.title: Long-Time Analysis of Stochastic Heavy Ball Dynamics for Convex Optimization and Monotone Equations
arxiv-2510-02951.creator: Radu Ioan Bo t ,, Chiara Schindler
arxiv-2510-02951.description: Abstract In a separable real Hilbert space, we study the problem of minimizing a convex function with Lipschitz continuous gradient in the presence of noisy evaluations. To this end, we associate a stochastic Heavy Ball system, incorporating a friction coefficient, with the optimization problem. We establish existence and uniqueness of trajectory solutions for this system.

arxiv-2601-01483.title: Unified Generation and Self-Verification for Vision-Language Models via Advantage Decoupled Preference Optimization
arxiv-2601-01483.creator: Xinyu Qiu, Heng Jia, Zhengwen Zeng, Shuheng Shen, Changhua Meng, Yi Yang, Linchao Zhu
arxiv-2601-01483.description: Abstract Parallel test-time scaling typically trains separate generation and verification models, incurring high training and inference costs. We propose Advantage Decoupled Preference Optimization ( ADPO ), a unified reinforcement learning framework that jointly learns answer generation and self-verification within a single policy.

pmc-10521540.title: A prospective analysis of physical activity and mental health in children: the GECKO Drenthe cohort
pmc-10521540.creator: Lu Yang, Eva Corpeleijn, Esther Hartman
pmc-10521540.description: BackgroundMental health problems in young people have become a global health burden. The positive effects of physical activity on mental health in adults are well known but still not clear in children. The aim of this study was to investigate to what extent physical activity in early childhood would affect mental health in middle childhood.

pmc-10578744.title: Prediction of reported monthly incidence of hepatitis B in Hainan Province of China based on SARIMA-BPNN model
pmc-10578744.creator: Kang Fang, Li Cao, Zhenwang Fu, Weixia Li
pmc-10578744.description: In recent years, the incidence of hepatitis B has been serious in Hainan Province of China. To construct a statistical model of the monthly incidence of hepatitis B in Hainan Province of China and predict the monthly incidence of hepatitis B in 2022.

pmc-11463140.title: The marine environmental microbiome mediates physiological outcomes in host nematodes
pmc-11463140.creator: Yiming Xue, Yusu Xie, Xuwen Cao, Liusuo Zhang
pmc-11463140.description: Background Nematodes are the most abundant metazoans in marine sediments, many of which are bacterivores; however, how habitat bacteria affect physiological outcomes in marine nematodes remains largely unknown. ResultsHere, we used a Litoditis marina inbred line to assess how native bacteria modulate host nematode physiology. We characterized seasonal dynamic bacterial compositions in L.

pmc-11545558.title: Impact of Drying Methods on Phenolic Composition and Bioactivity of Celery, Parsley, and Turmeric—Chemometric Approach
pmc-11545558.creator: Staniša Latinović, Ladislav Vasilišin, Lato Pezo, Nataša Lakić-Karalić, Dragoljub Cvetković, Aleksandra Ranitović, Sara Brunet, Teodora Cvanić, Jelena Vulić, Maomao Zeng
pmc-11545558.description: Drying is one of the most commonly used methods for food preservation, and in spice processing, it has a significant impact on quality. In this paper, the influences of drying at room temperature, 60 °C, and 90 °C and freeze-drying on celery and parsley roots and turmeric rhizomes were examined.

pmc-11678010.title: The Motility of Mouse Spermatozoa Changes Differentially After 30-Minute Exposure Under Simulating Weightlessness and Hypergravity
pmc-11678010.creator: Irina V Ogneva, Yulia S Zhdankina, Ksenia K Gogichaeva, Artyom A Malkov, Nikolay S Biryukov, Haim Breitbart
pmc-11678010.description: Research into the mechanisms by which gravity influences spermatozoa has implications for maintaining the species in deep space exploration and may provide new approaches to reproductive technologies on Earth. Changes in the speed of mouse spermatozoa after 30 min exposure to simulated weightlessness (by 3D-clinostat) and 2 g hypergravity (by centrifugation) were studied using inhibitory analysis.

pmc-12426188.title: Impact of electronic cigarette use and sleep duration, sleep issues and insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12426188.creator: Huma Sulthana, Asif Jan, Amogh Verma, Ranjana Sah, Rachana Mehta, Aftab Ullah, Abdur Rahim, Mohammad R. Alqudimat, Asmat Ullah
pmc-12426188.description: BackgroundThe increasing popularity of electronic cigarettes (e-cigarettes) has introduced new public health challenges and concerns. While promoted as safer alternatives to conventional tobacco and as tools for quitting smoking, e-cigarettes have raised alarm about possible long-term health consequences. This systematic review and meta-analysis sought to evaluate the association between electronic cigarette consumption and sleep disturbances.

pmc-12464195.title: Neural structural underlying audiovisual working memory and visual dominance under cognitive load
pmc-12464195.creator: Li Jiayu, Zhang Qiuzhu, Li Wenjuan, Zhang Junjun, Jin Zhenlan, Li Ling
pmc-12464195.description: Audiovisual working memory (WM) plays a critical role in multisensory cognitive processing, yet its structural neural correlates remain insufficiently understood. This study employed an audiovisual dual n-back task paradigm and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to investigate gray matter volume (GMV) associations with behavioral performance in 60 healthy individuals.

pmc-12734546.title: Why and How Are Infants with Hutchinson–Gilford Progeria Syndrome Born Without Severe Manifestations?
pmc-12734546.creator: Mariia A Erokhina, Ekaterina A Vorotelyak, Andrey V Vasiliev, Vepa K Abdyev, Kerstin Boengler, Steven R Goodman
pmc-12734546.description: Children with Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS) are born without height and weight abnormalities, and postnatal development is delayed from two months of age. The pathophysiological manifestations of HGPS can be categorized into the three tissue systems that are primarily affected: bone and cartilage, the smooth muscular layer of the vasculature, and the dermis layer.

pmc-13179159.title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Earth observation: human rights and the EU AI act
pmc-13179159.creator: Caroline Margaux Gevaert, Sanja Šćepanović, Nadia Bernaz, Hannes Taubenböck, Mrinalini Kochupillai
pmc-13179159.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems into Earth Observation (EO) research and innovation has catalyzed significant advancements in environmental monitoring, humanitarian response, and urban planning. However, these developments also raise novel regulatory and ethical challenges, particularly in light of the European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act (EU AI Act), which introduces a tiered risk-based framework for the governance of AI systems.

pmc-13236955.title: Survival outcomes, determinants, and hemodynamic trajectories with intravenous β1-selective blockade in septic shock complicated by tachyarrhythmia: a real-world MIMIC-IV cohort study
pmc-13236955.creator: Guoxiang Zou, Xiujuan Chen, Xuanhui Chen, Shuai Huang, Feier Song, Bei Hu, Guangjian Liu, Xin Li, Huixian Li
pmc-13236955.description: BackgroundSepsis and septic shock impose severe cardiovascular stress characterized by sympathetic overactivation and detrimental tachycardia, which is strongly linked to poor outcomes. While ultra-short-acting β1-blockers have shown promise in controlled trials for heart rate (HR) control, a critical gap remains regarding the optimal β1-selective regimen for complex, multimorbid, vasopressor-dependent patients with septic shock complicated by tachyarrhythmia in real-world settings.

pmc-13539906.title: Mapping the Evolutionary Landscape of Solid Tumor Immunotherapy: A Quarter-Century Bibliometric Analysis of the Title-Defined Core Literature (2000-2025)
pmc-13539906.creator: Ender Eren OZCELIK, Gul AKIN, Hulya ODABASI BUKUN, Mursel SALI, Ahmet Bilgehan SAHIN, Adem DELIGONUL, Erdem CUBUKCU, Turkkan EVRENSEL

pmc-13569815.title: Immune-sparing radiotherapy in solid tumors: radiation-induced lymphopenia, circulating immune-cell dose, and biomarker-guided optimization of radioimmunotherapy
pmc-13569815.creator: Shiduo Yang, E Erdemutu, Yuan Ren, Xinyu Jia, Qiaochu Ding, Chang Yang, Yu Lin
pmc-13569815.description: PurposeRadiotherapy is a central component of solid tumor management and can enhance antitumor immunity through antigen release, immunogenic cell death, innate immune activation, and tumor microenvironment remodeling. However, radiotherapy can also induce systemic immune injury by depleting circulating lymphocytes and irradiating lymphoid organs.

pmc-13584421.title: Age-related differences in pediatric anaphylaxis: a single-center experience
pmc-13584421.creator: Enes Çelik, Hande Yüksel Bulut
pmc-13584421.description: BackgroundPediatric anaphylaxis is a potentially life-threatening systemic hypersensitivity reaction with age-related differences in triggers and clinical manifestations. Real-life data are important to improve recognition, risk assessment, and management. This study aimed to evaluate the demographic and clinical characteristics, triggers, management, and factors associated with moderate-to-severe anaphylaxis in children, with particular emphasis on age-related differences.

pmc-13644262.title: Leucettine L41 Ameliorates Tau pathology and neuroinflammation in Parkinson’s disease models
pmc-13644262.creator: Subin Hwang, Hyunha Choi, Hyeyeon Cho, Sunjoo Ahn, Hwi-yeol Yun, Jin Sook Song
pmc-13644262.description: BackgroundAberrant protein phosphorylation and sustained neuroinflammatory activation are key biochemical features of experimental parkinsonism. Dysregulated tau processing and excessive microglial reactivity have been implicated in motor dysfunction associated with dopaminergic injury. In the present study, we evaluated the biochemical and functional effects of Leucettine L41 using biochemical, cellular, and in vivo systems.

wells-ann-veronica-1909.creator: H. G. Wells
